items.title: Premier League joins top European leagues in call for reforms to way Fifa is run
items.summary: Four leagues says Fifa governance ‘not fit for purpose’ They criticise ‘expansionism’ and want more input The Premier League has joined forces with La Liga, Serie A and the Bundesliga to call for urgent governance reform at Fifa after the World Cup sell-off debacle (FFE) as Gianni Infantino prepares to seek a fourth term as president. Their strongly worded statement is the latest indication that Infantino’s willingness to hold an external governance review does not go far enough, after the Guardian revealed that several Fifa council members ha ve rejected that proposal .

items.title: Guardiola sends message to Man City amid calls for titles to be taken away
items.summary: ‘I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club’ Former City chair Bernstein calls for directors to quit Pep Guardiola has thrown his support behind Manchester City after the club were found guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, telling fans: “We will get through this together.” Guardiola left City in the summer after a trophy-laden decade in charge, with his first two seasons falling within the period investigated by the independent commission. The Spaniard remains a close ally of the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, who brought him to England, the pair having previously worked together at Barcelona. City maintain their innocence and are set to appeal against the decision before Friday’s deadline.

items.title: How Man City's 'disguised funding scheme' changed the football landscape

items.title: Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto no longer a protected witness in Portugal
items.summary: Work provided information concerning City’s finances He called City decision ‘historic for English football’ Rui Pinto, whose leaks of private documents helped to trigger the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs, will no longer be protected as a witness by the Portuguese authorities, it can be revealed. The removal of the whistleblower’s protection was decided on Wednesday, according to documents seen by the Guardian. Pinto has also been advised to “exercise caution with family contacts” and avoid social media.

There is no prospect yet of Tuchel having to consider life without Kane.

items.title: Nations League roundup: Lamine Yamal sinks Croatia in Spain’s World Cup homecoming
items.summary: Teenager scores twice in 4-1 win to boost Ballon d’Or case Slovenia beat North Macedonia; Faroe Islands hold Moldova Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the World Cup. Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring within two minutes against England in Saturday’s Wembley win and took just 75 seconds to do so against Slaven Bilic’s side in Andalusia. The teenager’s left-footed finish took his tally of international goals to nine in 36 appearances.

items.title: Rival clubs feel relegating Manchester City to Championship would not be enough
items.summary: Premier League executives push for severe punishment City maintain they are ‘innocent of the accusations’ The Premier League will face pressure from Manchester City’s rivals to push for a sanction that will result in a prolonged absence from the top flight after the club were found guilty of more than 100 charges of financial rule-breaking. Executives at a number of Premier League clubs have told the Guardian that a points deduction that would relegate City to the Championship for a single season would be insufficient given the scale of what an independent commission described as the club’s “disguised funding scheme” and “sham commercial deals” , which enabled them to artificially inflate their income by £900m between 2009 and 2018.
